description: Height to normal for both methods of Painter 12.1.5 (Sharp, Smooth (Sobel)) and the virtual normal maps Normal_OpenGL / Normal_DirectX: the stencils on the Height read-out, the reoriented combination with the Normal mesh map and the Normal channel (at any coverage, both conventions), the scale at 256 to 2048 px, the encoding to 16 bits, fitted on the Tier 0 height-normal goldens, blend-normal-channel and the recordings of decision 077.

entries.subject: Normal_OpenGL and Normal_DirectX virtual maps from the Height channel, method Sharp (the default)
entries.formula: Input: the Height read-out before its write rule (the root layers composited from a transparent start, colour and coverage written half toward zero after each layer, then over the base 0 as fma(C - base, a, base): at opacity 0.75 and 0.1 the stored half is not what the stencil reads). Rows top first, wrap-around at the texture borders, h(dx, dy) the height at column + dx, row + dy. Sharp: v = (h(-1, 0) - h(0, 0), h(0, 0) - h(0, -1), 0.390625) in float32 (256 px). H = normalise(v); A = normalise(reoriented(F, H)), F = (0, 0, 1) without a Normal mesh map (height-normal-mesh-normal-map); C = decode(X) of the Normal channel's root list X at full coverage, the flat normal for an empty channel (height-normal-channel-coverage); n = normalise(reoriented(A, C)). normalise(v) = v rsqrt(fma(z, z, fma(x, x, y y))) with the recording GPU's float32 rsqrt (src/evaluator/hwmath.h); decode(c) = normalise(2c - 1, z clamped to >= 0); reoriented(b, d): t = b + (0, 0, 1), u = d (-1, -1, 1), e = fma(t.z, u.z, fma(t.y, u.y, t.x u.x)), r = (fma(t.x, e, -(u.x t.z)), fma(t.y, e, -(u.y t.z)), t.z (e - u.z)) (fma: the exact product plus z in double, rounded to float32). Normal_OpenGL = UNORM16(fma(n, 1/2, 1/2)); Normal_DirectX negates n.y first. UNORM16(e): e truncated to 20 fractional bits, then the nearest code, ties down.

entries.notes: Every r1 map, and every r2 map that equals its r1 (plane-strength s1 and s4 differ after save and reopen: height-normal-save-reopen-divergence). Domains: the plane grids compare the whole image, borders included (the wrap-around is exercised there); the sphere and the bevelled cube their UV coverage eroded by one texel (58816 and 51040 texels; outside it the export holds padding). The amplitude sweep stands in for a strength setting Painter 12.1.5 does not have (decision 047): the vector is linear in the height, with no other scale. Search (decisions 064): (-k dx, k dy, 1), k = 2.56, leaves 600+ texels one code off over the sweep; one normalisation of v alone 657, reoriented onto the flat normal with v as detail only (rnm(F, H)) 655 and with H as base only (rnm(H, F)) 359; the two reorientations leave none. For Sobel the float32 summation order is not separated by the goldens (an exact sum and this order both match every texel); this order is the implemented convention. Other set sizes scale z as 256 / W (height-normal-resolution-scaling).

entries.subject: Normal_OpenGL and Normal_DirectX virtual maps from the Height channel, method Smooth (Sobel)
entries.formula: Input: the Height read-out before its write rule (the root layers composited from a transparent start, colour and coverage written half toward zero after each layer, then over the base 0 as fma(C - base, a, base): at opacity 0.75 and 0.1 the stored half is not what the stencil reads). entries.subject: The Normal channel in the virtual map: the last detail of the combination
entries.formula: With a flat Height, Normal_OpenGL = UNORM16(fma(n, 1/2, 1/2)), n = normalise(reoriented(A, decode(C))), A = normalise(reoriented(F, normalise(0, 0, 0.390625))), C the Normal channel read-out (here its exported RGB16F value: full coverage, so the read-out over the flat colour is that value). The channel stores an imported normal map as (r, 65535 - g, b) / 65535 written half toward zero (blend-modes.json blend-normal-channel-import).

entries.subject: The Height channel's read-out (EXR export) of the amplitude sweep and the meshes
entries.formula: The exported Height is the read-out of height-normal-sharp written half toward zero: a bitmap fill stores half toward zero of float32(2 t) - 1, t = float32(code / 65535); a fill at opacity a over the transparent start keeps its colour and the coverage half(a); LinearDodge copies over a covered accumulator add, the sum written half toward zero; the read-out fma(C - 0, a, 0) is written half toward zero.

entries.subject: Empty Normal channel (no layer) exported as OpenEXR 32f: its base value

entries.subject: A Normal mesh map in the virtual maps (OpenGL and DirectX projects, both methods)
entries.formula: The bound Normal mesh map is F, the first base: F = decode(M), M = float32(code / 65535) of its 16-bit codes, its y negated when the map is in the DirectX convention (a map imported into a project takes the project's convention); A = normalise(reoriented(F, H)); n = normalise(reoriented(A, C)) as in height-normal-sharp. The exported mesh map (meshMap/normal_base) is the bitmap's codes unchanged in either project (the geometry-only pass-through in the map's own convention).

entries.subject: The Normal channel at partial coverage: its read-out and its normal in the virtual maps
entries.formula: The channel's layers composite over the flat colour B = (0.5, 0.5, 1) (its read-out, exported: half toward zero of fma(X - B, a, B)), while an empty channel exports the template base 127/255 (height-normal-default-normal-channel-base). The virtual maps read the root list from a transparent start, colour X and coverage a = half toward zero of opacity x mask: C = (0, 0, 1) where a = 0, decode(X) where a = 1, else u = decode(X rcp(a)) turned toward (0, 0, 1) by a: (u.x k, u.y k, cos(t)), t = a acos(z), z = u.z clamped to [0, 1], k = sin(t) rsqrt(fma(-z, z, 1)); rcp, acos, sin, cos and rsqrt are the recording GPU's (the acos its Vulkan arccosine: 2 P(sqrt(fma(-1/2, z, 1/2))) for z > 0.57, else float32(pi/2) - P(z), P the arcsine polynomial of hwmath.h).

entries.subject: 8- and 16-bit normal maps on the Normal channel of OpenGL and DirectX projects
entries.formula: The channel stores an imported normal map as (r, max - g, b) / max written half toward zero in both conventions (8 and 16 bits); the virtual maps read that storage. A DirectX project's export of a non-empty Normal channel inverts the stored green again: half toward zero of 1 - g; an empty channel exports 127/255 in both.
